title: Structured resonances and avalanche diagnostics in the quasiperiodic XXZ chain
statement: For the spin-1/2 nearest-neighbor XXZ chain with Delta=1, h_j=W_A cos(2 pi beta j+phi_A), beta=(sqrt(5)-1)/2, and an implanted quasiperiodic bath with W_B=0.5 in exchange units, determine whether structured resonances explain the disagreement between correlation-based and particle-number-entropy avalanche diagnostics. Quantify their effect on bath coupling, or identify where this proposed explanation fails.
source_locator: SRC-PHYS-001 sections II, V.2 and VI; SRC-PHYS-002 section V.3.
status_basis: The originating paper explicitly requests a resonance-sensitive coupling description. Later work discusses structural rare regions without resolving this diagnostic discrepancy; no matching resolution was located.
plain_summary: A small thermal region may erase memory in an otherwise localized quantum chain. Two diagnostics disagree about its spread; the source asks how quasiperiodic resonances change the explanation.
assumptions: Use spin operators S=sigma/2, not unscaled Pauli matrices; the exchange is J(SxSx+SySy+Delta SzSz), with J=Delta=1.
Match the source diagnostics using a zero-magnetization Neel state and phases phi_A, phi_B sampled uniformly in [0,2 pi); the bath field is W_B cos(2 pi beta j+phi_B), W_B=0.5.
Specify chain and bath lengths. Boundary conditions were not confirmed in this inspection and must be checked before reproducing the simulations.
State assumptions about the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), local integrals of motion and weak coupling separately from exact Hamiltonian identities.
scope: The source's quantitative mechanism question. It is not the general existence problem for many-body localization.
target: A controlled test of the proposed resonance mechanism and its consequences for the two diagnostics in the stated Hamiltonian.
success_criteria: State a quantitative claim, its approximations and a reproducible comparison with independent calculations.
Separate finite-size agreement from an asymptotic theorem; identify what remains unexplained.
Check later literature before describing any explanation or parameter regime as new.
known_results: SRC-PHYS-001 reports finite-chain disagreement between correlation and particle-number-entropy diagnostics and leaves coupling renormalization open. Resonance-driven coupling renormalization is the authors' proposed explanation, not an established mechanism.
SRC-PHYS-002 discusses structural rare regions without establishing that they initiate the required avalanche.
prerequisites: Perturbation theory and numerical error analysis
significance: A quantitative connection between microscopic dynamics and thermalization diagnostics would strengthen interpretation of localization studies.
